A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoSMIC/VTI research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations for robust variable selection and nonlinear DAG discovery, plus analysis of Sachs flow-cytometry data.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical studies and reports expanded DAG baseline comparisons and revised results.

M1.justification: The proposed CoSMIC masking, permutations, flow compositions, model samplers, gradient estimator, and information-gain step control remain unchanged. The added discussion of beta=0 concerns the existing surrogate formula; no new implemented method component is established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate robust variable selection across the same misspecification, prior, and cardinality scenarios, synthetic 10-node DAGs, and the same Sachs dataset. The cardinality sweep already appears in v1's appendix; newly mentioned application domains are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The synthetic DAG comparison expands from DAGMA alone to DAGMA, DiBS, DiBS+, and JSP-GFlowNets (v1 Figure 3; v2 Figure 4). Sachs Table 1 adds DiBS+ and JSP-GFN. This substantially broadens the comparison to include Bayesian alternatives.

E3.justification: The added baseline evaluations introduce specified protocols: DiBS/DiBS+ uses 5,000 steps and 10 particles, while JSP-GFN uses 50,000 iterations with batch size 1,024. Added real-data baselines use 10 hidden nodes without biases. The retained VTI settings and evaluation metrics remain stable.

E4.justification: The existing cardinality-sensitivity study reports revised cross-entropy distributions across model-space sizes in v2 Figure 3, beyond its relocation from v1 Figure 4. Its underlying question is retained, as are the flow-expressivity and prior/misspecification analyses, including unchanged plots in Figures 5–10.

E5.justification: The DAG simulation caption changes from 10 repetitions to nine, although v2 Appendix G.4 still states 10 datasets, leaving the actual aggregation count inconsistent. Mean/standard-error reporting and 10 VTI optimization seeds remain. V1's disclosure of 1,024 RJMCMC replicate chains disappears.

E6.justification: Under retained stated VTI settings, Sachs Table 1 changes VTI's F1 from 0.61 to 0.44, SHD and Brier from 15 to 23, and AUROC from 0.79 to 0.68; DAGMA's row is unchanged. Synthetic DAG curves and cardinality-sweep distributions are revised. Added baseline results include DiBS+'s best Sachs Brier score of 17.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the regression likelihood by centering the Gaussian components at the regression mean, and corrects the RJMCMC death acceptance probability in Appendix F.3. Core factorization and convergence proofs are retained. Section 3.1 adds a recursive-GP cost analysis and permits beta=0, although Appendix C retains a positive-beta assumption.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a single amortized transdimensional variational density through CoSMIC flows, a VTI framework with surrogate and Monte Carlo approaches, convergence guarantees, and applicability to large model spaces. The reparameterization-trick explanation clarifies the retained contribution.

C2.justification: V2 changes small-model-space advice from recommending the GP sampler to allowing categorical Monte Carlo gradients as a safe default. It adds discussion of mode collapse and cross-model information sharing. Appendix G explains DAGMA's selection using the true edge count and VTI's sparsity-prior tuning toward the Sachs consensus graph.

D1.justification: V1 promises future code availability; v2 reports that code is available. V2 documents added baseline budgets and DAGMA's output-selection criterion. Conversely, v1's RJMCMC chain-length, thinning, retained-sample, and replicate-chain details are not retained when the cardinality discussion moves into the main text.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for DiBS, JSP-GFlowNets, additional transdimensional applications, and flow comparisons. New Remark C.4 positions the convergence result against Oliveira et al. (2021), emphasizing differing assumptions and nonstationary targets. The main related-work section's positioning remains largely intact.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting spans the introduction, optimization motivation, experimental narrative, and Discussion. CoSMIC implementation and proofs are separated into appendices, the categorical-distribution proposition moves out of the main text, and the cardinality study becomes part of the main experimental narrative.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 2, and 11 are revised visually. V2 Figure 3 combines the relocated cardinality plots with selected posterior panels, while the DAG figure and Table 1 expand for additional baselines. Axes, legends, captions, and the placement of appendix figures are extensively reworked.

improvement.justification: Adding Bayesian DAG baselines addresses v1's reliance on DAGMA alone, while corrected likelihood and acceptance formulas improve technical correctness. Clearer explanations and disclosure of tuning choices improve interpretability. These gains are limited by removed RJMCMC sampling details and the new nine-versus-ten repetition inconsistency. Overall, v2 offers a modest improvement in evidential breadth and transparency.
